Act as the research sub-agent for this task.

You are an advisor. Decide which proposed changes to the inkling repo's AGENTS.md are worth making. DO NOT edit, create, or delete any file, and do not run git write commands. Read-only. The parent agent will implement whatever you approve.

Repo: C:\Users\chris\.t3\worktrees\inkling\t3-5f0fda84 (an Electron/React/TS/SQLite Windows app called inkling). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root first, including its stated taste: "simple software that feels obvious beats impressive machinery", yagni, fight scope creep, document only what a maintainer would get wrong without it, no file catalogs, default to no comment. Judge every item against that bar.

inkling's AGENTS.md was forked from t3code's (pingdotgg/t3code). Fetch theirs with: gh api repos/pingdotgg/t3code/contents/AGENTS.md -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"   (for the git.cafe item also: gh api repos/pingdotgg/t3code/contents/docs/operations/development.md -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"). Do not pull in t3code's remote/mobile/evals/dev-auth material; it does not apply.

Decide each item below: ADOPT, SKIP, or ADOPT-MODIFIED. For each give a one or two sentence reason grounded in what you actually found in the code. For every ADOPT or ADOPT-MODIFIED, give the exact final text to insert and the exact existing line/section it goes after or replaces (quote an anchor from the current AGENTS.md). Keep proposed text as short as the existing style allows.

Items:
A. Effect conventions. electron/ has used Effect since commit #187 (about 17 files import "effect"; see electron/ai-jobs.ts, electron/storage/context.ts, electron/main.ts and the typed IPC contracts in packages/contracts). AGENTS.md says nothing about it. t3code's AGENTS.md has Effect.fn / thin-transport / services guidance. Read the real code to see what conventions inkling actually follows, and propose only a rule that matches reality and that an agent would otherwise get wrong. Skip if there is no such rule.
B. A "check changed files" script analogous to t3code's `vp run check:changed`. AGENTS.md currently says "targeted lint and typecheck for the scope you changed" with no command. Look at package.json scripts, t3.json (AGENTS.md says to keep t3.json in sync with scripts), and .github/workflows/ci.yml. Is a small script worth adding, or is the right fix just naming the existing commands in the Verifying section? If a script, give the exact package.json entry; if just docs, the exact text.
C. Lint enforcement of test rules. AGENTS.md prose bans fixed sleeps, per-test timeouts, retries, Date.now/performance.now deltas, polling loops, and unreasoned skips in tests. t3code backs these with lint rules. Look at oxlint-plugin-inkling/ and how rules are written/tested there. Which of these, if any, are cheap and reliable enough to enforce as rules, versus staying as prose? Do not implement; say which to build and roughly how big each is.
D. git.cafe mirror. The maintainer has a git.cafe mirror of this repo. In this worktree `git remote -v` shows only origin = https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling.git and nothing in docs/ mentions cafe. t3code's AGENTS.md has a rule ("If origin is git.cafe, follow GitCafe mirror ... push to origin, open and track PRs with `cafe` and their git.cafe URLs, keep gh for merging") backed by a docs/operations/development.md section. Should inkling add an equivalent? If yes, list exactly what facts are still unknown and must be asked of the maintainer (remote name, URL form, cafe CLI) rather than guessed, and say whether to add nothing until they are known.
E. Tracker contradictions in AGENTS.md. The "Plans and work artifacts" section says active work is tracked in "the GitHub issue or project item", while the "Linear issues" section says the Linear issue is the tracker, "not roadmap.md", then also says to tick the roadmap.md box and add a changelog line, and "don't keep a second checklist". Check docs/roadmap.md and docs/changelog.md (and recent git log) to see how they are actually used, then propose the minimal consistent rewrite and say which source of truth should win.
F. Rot-prone specifics: "Where code lives" has "the 48 item corpus" and a `docs/` catalog line ("docs/ holds product, behavior, stack, roadmap, and changelog. No other docs home exists yet."), which conflicts with the file's own rule against file catalogs. Verify whether the 48 count is still true and whether the docs line says anything the Documentation section does not. Remove, fix, or keep?
G. The sentence "If a rule here fights the task in front of you, say so..." appears twice (end of "A note on taste" and the last bullet of "Taste"). Which to keep?
H. "Hit every surface" always asks the agent to walk the whole list. Is a one-line scoping note (so a pure UI tweak does not recite Capture paths and Search paths) worth adding?

Finish with a compact table: item letter, verdict, and the one-line summary. Put the exact insertion text under each item above the table. No preamble.

 ## Dev servers
 
-- `bun install` installs. If module resolution looks broken, check the Bun version first. It must match `.bun-version` (1.4.2). `bun run check:bun-version` says so in one line.
+- `bun install` installs. If module resolution looks broken, run `bun run check:bun-version`.
 - `bun run dev` is the quick web look at the UI. It uses sample data and has no desktop storage or processing backend.
 - `bun run dev:app` opens the Electron shell in preview mode. The renderer shows the sample library and does not call the desktop backend, so capture, OCR, embeddings, and local file access are not exercised there. Test the full backend with the packaged output of `bun run build:dir`.

@@ -103,8 +103,10 @@ An empty library is a bad test. Seed your run with a copy of real data instead o
 - A test earns its place by guarding something that breaks quietly: extraction and sanitizing, embed allowlists, OCR scoring, queue leases and recovery, migrations and persistence, asset path containment and range requests, deep link and external-format parsing, ordering and race guarantees, and `liquidGlassShape`. A test added with a bug fix stays; mark it `// regression: #NNN` if its name doesn't say so.
 - Don't write tests the types already prove, trivial logic, basic DOM behavior, static-markup renders, mock-call mirrors, smoke tests, duplicate table rows, or wall-clock and perf asserts.
 - Ingestion and background changes ship with focused tests for that behavior. A behavior change with no test is unfinished.
+- Proof for a bug fix depends on the bug. Logic, data, state, and protocol bugs get a failing test first (the fewest that fail on `main` for that reason), then the fix. Purely visual bugs (spacing, colour, alignment, a layout shift) get before/after captures and no test.
+- Extend before you add. When an existing test or table covers the behavior, add a row or an assertion there. Write a new `it` only when no case fits. Test at the lowest layer that fails on `main`, not again in a wrapper or at each call site.
 - Background work is async. Await the real signal: a job drain, a lease state, an event. No fixed sleeps, per-test timeouts, retries, `Date.now()` or `performance.now()` deltas, polling loops, or skips without a reason.
-- UI changes need one real pass in the running app before you call them done. Preview for layout, full app for anything native. Take a screenshot through the harness so the user can see it. The primary agent does this once after integrating. Subagents do not launch their own dev servers. Clean up what you launched when you are done.
+- UI changes need one real pass in the running app before you call them done (the `verify-inkling` skill drives it). Preview for layout, full app for anything native. Take a screenshot through the harness so the user can see it. The primary agent does this once after integrating. Subagents do not launch their own dev servers. Clean up what you launched when you are done.
 - Electron and frontend changes get focused tests, typecheck, and changed-file `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`. There are no local hooks — CI runs the frontend checks and Electron package smoke tests.
 
 ## Pull requests
@@ -115,7 +117,7 @@ An empty library is a bad test. Seed your run with a copy of real data instead o
 - UI changes need before/after images. Motion or timing needs a short video.
 - Upload PR evidence to GitHub. Never commit PR-only screenshots or assets such as `.github/pr-assets/`.
 - One request is one PR. Split it only when the maintainer asks.
-- When babysitting: poll checks and comments newer than the last push, verify each bot finding against the source, fix real ones, dismiss false positives with a written reason. Stay quiet when nothing is new. Stop when the bots are green on the latest commit.
+- When babysitting: call `watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you on checks, comments, or conflicts. Do not poll or sleep. Verify each bot finding against the source, fix real ones, dismiss false positives with a written reason. Stay quiet when nothing is new. Stop when the bots are green on the latest commit.
 
 ## Linear issues
 
@@ -136,7 +138,7 @@ Most code changes need no docs change. Agents can read the code.
 - Keep a local implementation explanation in a nearby code comment. Use an internal doc when the reasoning crosses boundaries or needs context the code cannot carry well. Link to the relevant source instead of copying it.
 - When a documented decision or constraint changes, rewrite or remove the affected text. Do not append another account of the new behavior. A new internal page needs a distinct, durable reason to exist.
 - Keep user docs in the shipped product's voice, without implementation details or contributor tooling. Update the relevant feature section when how to use it changes. A UI tweak does not need a documentation entry, and a new control does not need its own page. A settings path is useful; descriptions of visible buttons, icons, layouts, animations, or every UI state are not. Before adding text, ask what task or decision it helps the user with.
-- The changelog rules live at the top of `docs/changelog.md` and still apply. One line per entry, grouped under Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Deprecated, Security. Trivial edits skip the changelog. Never write that an agent did the work.
+- The changelog rules live at the top of `docs/changelog.md` and still apply. One line per entry, grouped under Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Deprecated, Security. Trivial edits skip the changelog.
 - `docs/operations/` holds maintainer setup, release, and debugging procedures. Keep instructions for operating an installed inkling version in the user guides.
 
 ## Plans and work artifacts
@@ -144,7 +146,6 @@ Most code changes need no docs change. Agents can read the code.
 - Do not commit implementation plans, research notes, or agent scratch files. Keep temporary working material outside the worktree. `.plans/` is gitignored only as a safety net for legacy tooling.
 - Track active maintainer work in the GitHub issue or project item that owns it. External proposals follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
 - A merged PR is the implementation record. Close or update its tracking item when the work lands; do not preserve a second checklist in the repository.
-- While completing work, keep `docs/changelog.md` current per its own header rules. Close out the entry before starting an unrelated task so entries do not blur together. Organize details in the Unreleased section as you work or if you notice that changes are piling up so it doesn't become messy. Always ask the developer before making those types of changes but do not ask after every change, only after important or large amounts of work are done.

# Changelog

All notable development phases and changes are recorded here. See also [roadmap.md](roadmap.md) for what comes next.

The best times to update this file so as to minimize friction while working with a developer or contributor are:
1. When completing a medium-large implementation pass of features, bug fixes, performance enhancements, refactoring updates, or likewise changes
2. The user indicates, whether directly or indirectly through their actions, they want to or are going to finish up the local work and merge the changes afterwards
3. Before starting a new, unrelated task — close out the entry for the work just finished rather than letting it blur or get jumbled into the next thing
4. When a change alters public behavior: API contracts, CLI flags, config options, env vars; anything a user of the project depends on being stable

Changelog entry format: 

- Follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/): group entries under `Added`, `Changed`, `Fixed`, `Removed`, `Deprecated`, `Security`.
- Each entry is one line, written for a human reader — what changed in simple technical terms that someone could understand with simple google searches, not a commit message or file diff summary.
- Reference issue/PR numbers or ticket IDs when they exist
- Keep an `Unreleased` section at the top; move entries under a version heading at release time

Guardrails:
- Never mention that changes were made by an AI agent or even a developer — write entries as if the changes were just made
- Don't editorialize or pad entries to look more substantial than the change was
- If a change is trivial (typo fix, formatting, comment-only), skip the changelog — not every commit needs an entry
- Ask before rewriting or reordering existing changelog history when you notice it is drifting from the required structure; only append.
- When restructuring this document NO important/crucial/technical details should be lost

# Development

How to set up, run, check, and troubleshoot inkling. Contribution scope and PR expectations live in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; this is the command and check reference.

## First-time setup

1. Install Bun 1.4.2 (pinned in `.bun-version` and `package.json#packageManager`).
2. `bun install` — plain install, no hooks and no lifecycle scripts.

## Running

| Goal | Command |
|---|---|
| Web look with sample data | `bun run dev` |
| Electron desktop app (dev) | `bun run dev:app` |
| Serve the last production build | `bun run preview` (run `bun run build` first) |
| Production frontend build (keeps demo seed) | `bun run build` |
| Shipped app build (drops demo seed) | `bun run build:app` |
| Electron directory build (unpacked) | `bun run build:dir` |
| Windows NSIS installer | `bun run build:installer` |

## A. Effect conventions: ADOPT-MODIFIED

inkling does the opposite of t3code here. `electron/` and `packages/` contain 63 `Effect.fnUntraced` calls and no `Effect.fn` at all. There is no tracer or OTel layer, `Effect.gen` is only used inline or to build layers, and services are `Context.Service` plus `Layer` (`electron/storage/library.ts:98`, `jobs.ts:292`). An agent that copies t3code's guidance or follows the Effect docs will reach for `Effect.fn`. The other rule an agent could break is "Effect stops at the IPC edge" (`main.ts:221` and `:355`). That rule is in `docs/tech-stack.md:28`, which AGENTS.md doesn't point to for Effect. Skip t3code's thin-transport and services material: inkling has one generic command handler, so there is nothing to get wrong there.

Insert this after `- Inferred types over annotations. \`any\` is the enemy.` in **Taste**:

```
- Effect stays in the main process and stops at the IPC edge; the renderer never imports it at runtime. Reusable Effect functions use `Effect.fnUntraced`, not `Effect.fn` (nothing collects spans). Keep `Effect.gen` for inline programs and layers.
```

## B. Check changed files: ADOPT-MODIFIED (docs only, no script)

A script isn't worth it. `typecheck` uses tsc-rs and is already fast across the whole repo. `lint` is just `oxlint && oxfmt --check`, and both tools accept file arguments. CI has no changed-files mode to mirror. A new script would also mean another entry in `t3.json`. What's actually missing is the command names. `check:refs` (`scripts/assert-command-refs.ts`) already checks every `bun run <x>` mentioned in AGENTS.md, so naming the commands won't rot quietly.

Replace this bullet in **Verifying**:
`- Smallest proof that the change works. \`bun test <files>\` for the tests you touched, targeted lint and typecheck for the scope you changed. The full check is ...`

with:

```
- Smallest proof that the change works: `bun test <files>` for the tests you touched, `bunx oxlint <files>` and `bunx oxfmt --check <files>` for what you changed, and `bun run typecheck` (fast enough to run whole). The full check is `bun run check`, which mirrors the CI frontend job. Do not run it unless you changed something broad or the user asked.
```

Then shorten the last Verifying bullet (`- Electron and frontend changes get focused tests, typecheck, and changed-file \`oxlint\` and \`oxfmt --check\`. There are no local hooks — ...`) to:

```
- There are no local hooks. CI runs the frontend checks and Electron package smoke tests.
```

Small fix in a different file, if you want it: `docs/operations/development.md:48` says typecheck covers "App + benchmark harness", but it also checks `electron/tsconfig.json`.

## C. Lint enforcement of test rules: ADOPT-MODIFIED (one small rule, the rest stays prose)

None of the 41 test files currently breaks any of these rules. My grep for `setTimeout`, `Bun.sleep`, `.skip`/`.todo`, `Date.now()`, `performance.now()` and timeout arguments only matched `retry` in job-queue domain code, which is legitimate. So the value of a rule is guarding against agents that bring t3code habits, nothing more. The plugin has two hand-written rules, 62 and 136 lines, and no rule tests. Build only the cases that can be matched purely on syntax:

- **Build `inkling/no-test-timeout-or-unreasoned-skip`**, roughly 50 to 70 lines in the style of `require-suppression-reason.ts`, scoped to `*.test.ts(x)`. It would flag:
  - a numeric or options third argument to `test`/`it`/`describe`
  - `.skip` or `.todo` without a `-- reason` comment on the line
  - `setTimeout` or `Bun.sleep` wrapped in a Promise inside test bodies
- **Keep as prose:**
  - `Date.now`/`performance.now` deltas: fixtures use timestamps legitimately, so this needs a heuristic to tell them apart.
  - Polling loops: they can't be detected reliably.
  - Retries: the word collides with the job-queue `retry` API.

If you want to stay strictly within yagni, skip even the one rule and revisit when a violation actually lands. I lean slightly toward building it, because it's cheap and agents will import these habits.

## D. git.cafe mirror: SKIP for now

Nothing in this repo points to cafe: `origin` is GitHub, and `docs/`, `.github/` and AGENTS.md never mention it. t3code's rule depends on a `development.md` section with real URLs and a CLI install line. Guessing those would produce instructions that send PRs to the wrong place. Add nothing until the maintainer confirms:

1. The mirror URL (for example `https://git.cafe/Squidys-Tools/inkling.git`) and whether it syncs both ways, with matching PR and issue numbers.
2. Whether agents should set `origin` to the cafe URL, or keep GitHub as `origin` and add a `cafe` remote. t3code's rule hinges on "if origin is git.cafe".
3. The `cafe` CLI version and auth setup they use, and whether `gh` stays the tool for merging (t3code's `--match-head-commit` reason).
4. Whether CI checks show up on cafe, and whether the bare `#n` link rewriting affects how `Fixes` references are written here.

Once those are answered, port t3code's one bullet into Pull requests plus a short "GitCafe mirror" section in `docs/operations/development.md`.

## E. Tracker contradictions: ADOPT-MODIFIED (Linear wins)

Here is how each source is actually used:

- **Linear:** it's the real tracker. `roadmap.md` and `changelog.md` both cite `SQU-*` IDs (`changelog.md` has 22).
- **GitHub issues:** they hold only automated Link Checker reports.
- **`roadmap.md`:** its own header calls it a milestone checklist of shipped work. Its job is "standing", per the Documentation section.
- **`changelog.md`:** the history.

So "tick roadmap.md" and "no second checklist" don't actually conflict: roadmap shows milestone standing, not per-task tracking. The wording just makes them look like they conflict.

Replace `- Track active maintainer work in the GitHub issue or project item that owns it. External proposals follow \`CONTRIBUTING.md\`.` with:

```
- Track active maintainer work in its Linear issue (see [Linear issues](#linear-issues)). External proposals follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
```

Replace `- A merged PR is the implementation record. Close or update its tracking item when the work lands; do not preserve a second checklist in the repository.` with:

```
- A merged PR is the implementation record. Do not keep a task checklist in the repository; `docs/roadmap.md` records milestone standing only.
```

In **Linear issues**, replace `- One Linear issue owns one task (e.g. \`SQU-6\`). That issue is the tracker — not \`roadmap.md\`, not a plan file.` with:

```
- One Linear issue owns one task (e.g. `SQU-6`). That issue is the tracker, not a plan file.
```

Also in **Linear issues**, replace `- If merged: move the issue to Done. A merged PR is the implementation record, don't keep a second checklist.` with:

```
- If merged: move the issue to Done.
```

Keep the "tick the roadmap box, add a changelog line" bullet as it is; it's now consistent. `docs/bugs.md`, which the roadmap header calls the list of open defects, is another possible second tracker. I'd flag that to the maintainer rather than change it here.

## F. Rot-prone specifics: ADOPT-MODIFIED

48 is still correct (`benchmarks/manifest.json` lists 48 IDs), but the number adds nothing and will go stale. The `docs/` line is already wrong: `docs/` also holds `bugs.md`, `design.md`, `models.md`, `README.md` and `operations/`, so "No other docs home exists yet" is false. The Documentation section already covers what that line says.

In **Where code lives**, replace `- \`benchmarks/\` holds the 48 item corpus, the harness, expected outputs, and results. Of the results, only \`results-latest.json\` and \`summary.md\` are tracked.` with:

```
- `benchmarks/` holds the corpus, the harness, expected outputs, and results. Of the results, only `results-latest.json` and `summary.md` are tracked.
```

Delete the line `- \`docs/\` holds product, behavior, stack, roadmap, and changelog. No other docs home exists yet.` entirely.

## G. Duplicate "If a rule here fights..." sentence: ADOPT

Keep the one at the end of **A note on taste**, which sits next to "good defaults… preferences should be able to override anything here". Delete the last bullet of **Taste**: `- If a rule here fights the task in front of you, say so loudly and get a human sign-off before breaking it.`

## H. Scoping note for "Hit every surface": ADOPT-MODIFIED

It's worth one clause. The intro already limits the list to "ingestion or display work", but "walk this list and say which entries applied" still pushes the agent to recite all of it. Replace `Before calling ingestion or display work done, walk this list and say which entries applied.` with:

```
Before calling ingestion or display work done, walk this list and name the entries that applied; skip the rest silently.
```
